note: Adapted from the original description of Sjöstedt (in German), published as Eutermes contractus n. sp.; the alate (called Königin in the original, body length 9 mm, noted as possibly not fully grown), large and small nasute soldiers and the worker are described; type locality Katanga, Welgelegen, Congo, 14 June 1912 (month 6) (collected by D. J. Bequaert). The BSF bibliography dates it to Sjöstedt 1913a, but volume 2 of the Revue Zoologique Africaine and the citation of Snyder (1949) give 1926, the pagination following Snyder being 355—356. The original places the species in Eutermes, now in Fulleritermes. The body length of the large nasute soldier is illegible in the scan and is not given.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Alate (called Königin in the original: queen / founding female): entirely dark brownish black to black, only the tibiae and tarsi slightly paler; abdominal intersegmental membrane whitish. Head oval, a quarter longer than the width between the outer margins of the eyes, with a small raised point in the middle; clypeus hardly paler than the frons, oval, anterior margin truncate; first two mandibular teeth almost equal; antennae 13-segmented, the basal segment slightly shorter than the following two together, segment 2 slightly longer than segment 3, segments 3 and 4 appearing equal, these two sometimes incompletely divided and fused into one, the distal segments nearly equal. Pronotum semicircular, anterior margin broadly concave, posterior part slightly flat; in natural position the pronotum about as wide as the head between the outer margins of the eyes; posterior margin of the mesonotum concave, the corners broadly rounded; posterior margin of the metanotum slightly concave; the first few abdominal tergites paler along the midline. Body length 9 mm (noted in the original as "probably not fully grown").

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Large nasute soldier: head yellow red, nasus dark; in dorsal view the head roundly triangular, the posterior margin a broad arc, characteristically constricted at the base of the nasus; in lateral view the head and the nasus form a straight line, the occiput distinctly higher and forming a very distinct obtuse angle with the straight nasus. Small nasute soldier: very similar to the large one, only slightly smaller, the obtuse angle between the top of the occiput and the nasus slightly larger; body length 3 mm, head length 1.35 mm, head width 0.67 mm. In the large one the body length is illegible because of corrupt typesetting in the scan, head length 1.62 mm, head width 0.67 mm (printed "6,7", which by the measurements of the small form of the same species should be 0.67).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Worker: head oval, slightly narrowed forwards, widest in the middle, reddish brown, with three distinct white lines meeting in the middle; clypeus concolorous with the head, broadly oval, twice as wide as long, anterior margin truncate, with a fine pale line along the midline; first two mandibular teeth equal; antennae dark brown with pale rings, 14-segmented, segment 4 the smallest, the basal segment equal to the following two together, segment 2 slightly longer than segment 4, the middle segments round and slightly longer than wide, the terminal segment slightly longer and narrower than the penultimate and slightly narrowed at the apex. Pronotum reddish brown, as is the mesonotum, with a fine white line along the midline; anterior lobe much larger than the posterior lobe, arcuate, not concave in the middle, only about 3/4 as long as the posterior lobe, the posterior lobe unusually small; dorsum of the abdomen dark brown, venter paler; legs pale, femora dark. Body length 4 mm, head width 0.75—0.82 mm.
